findings: FINDING (S01): after a wrong-password attempt, the blocking 'document_password_required' reconciliation case stays OPEN even once the correct password succeeds, so the position parses but is left status='reconciliation_required' with blocking reason 'open_blocking_reconciliation_case'. Nothing in processSourceDocument resolves that case on a later successful extraction of the same document. Observed truth row: [{"status":"reconciliation_required","blocking_reasons":[{"code":"open_blocking_reconciliation_case","message":"An unresolved blocking-severity reconciliation case exists for this position."}]}].

cases.name: Folio statement first, then an overlapping CAS: no economic duplication, and order-independent

checks.label: the folio-statement import succeeded
the AMC-blind folio statement created one account under the Unknown AMC sentinel
OBSERVATION: which identifiers the AMC-blind (FS1-first) import preserved
the CAS import succeeded
the CAS adopted and upgraded the SAME account rather than creating a second one for the same folio
both documents resolved to exactly ONE canonical instrument
the overlapping transaction exists exactly ONCE and the CAS-only transaction was added: 2 rows, not 3
OBSERVATION: whether the later CAS (which DOES print the ISIN) backfills the identifier onto the already-minted instrument
BOTH orders produce the identical economic shape: 1 account, 1 instrument, 2 transactions

antiVacuityControl.label: the same row counter rose from 1 to 2 across the second import (dedup suppressed the duplicate only, not the new row)

findings: FINDING (S05): the folio statement printed ISIN INZZ1IUNP056 in its FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS section, but the instrument minted from it carries isin=null and identifier rows []. documentProcessing.ts builds uniqueSchemes keyed by (normalisedName|plan|option|amc) and writes the TRANSACTION scheme first, then OVERWRITES it with the HOLDING scheme — and camsFolioStatementParser.parseHoldings deliberately emits buildScheme(name, null) because the Summary of Holdings block prints no ISIN. The globally-unique identifier present in the source document is therefore dropped for any FS1-first import. Subsequent resolution still lands on the same instrument (via normalised name + plan/option + country), so this is a lost-identifier defect, not a duplication defect.

FINDING (S05, continued): the ISIN is NOT recovered later either. After the CAS import — which prints ISIN INZZ1IUNP056 and resolves to this same instrument via normalised name — the instrument still carries isin=null and identifier rows []. schemeResolution's 'resolved' branch only MAPS to the existing instrument; only the 'unresolved' branch writes ii_instrument_identifiers. So an FS1-first position is permanently left without the ISIN that both of its source documents printed, and any future statement that carries ONLY an ISIN (no matching scheme name) would mint a SECOND instrument for the same real fund.

cases.name: A document whose own arithmetic does not close is BLOCKED, never certified

checks.label: the import ran to completion (the pipeline did not simply crash)
the non-closing position was BLOCKED (status reconciliation_required)
the blocking reason names the arithmetic: 'unit_variance_exceeds_tolerance'
the recorded variance is the real arithmetic difference (50 reconstructed vs 250 printed = -200)
the blocked position was never certified (certified_at is null)

antiVacuityControl.label: in the SAME import, the arithmetically correct position DID reach a certified state (so this is discrimination, not a blanket block)

cases.name: The same position contributes to net worth exactly once, not once per source document

checks.label: the two-document position has exactly ONE canonical position row, not one per document
there is at most ONE holding snapshot per as-of date (a second document for the same date cannot add a second snapshot)
the position value carried forward is the statement closing balance (100 units), NOT the sum of both documents (150)
publishing the FIRST document's position is accepted
the database REFUSES to also publish the SECOND document's position for the same (account, instrument) — net worth cannot count it twice

evidence.secondInsert: rejected 23505: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uidx_ii_fhip_publications_one_active_position"

checks.label: the same second position IS accepted with status superseded — the constraint targets two SIMULTANEOUSLY ACTIVE publications, not any second row

antiVacuityControl.label: the same query without the position filter reports many positions for this user (the "exactly 1" is a genuine filter, not an empty table)
